meta.language: en-US - faithful translation of the Portuguese source; card texts already in English are verbatim
meta.rule: Do not invent ideas, titles, times or materials. This file is the single source of truth for Designer and Developer.

approval.timeMessAgeRoom: from the PDF cards, machine-verified against the PDF's own totals
approval.typeTags: PENDING OWNER APPROVAL (Gate 2) - arrival, goodbye, project and interactive are fixed by the PDF; funny and cute are proposed by the PM
approval.materialTags: PENDING OWNER APPROVAL (Gate 2) - proposed by the PM, not in the PDF
approval.note: Do not build filters, /funny/ or Tonight Mode on typeTags/materialTags until they are approved.

fields.editorNotes: Internal. Never rendered on the site.
fields.illustrationBrief: Internal. Brief for the illustrator; never rendered on the site.
fields.elfNote: null = the PDF has no ready text; do not render the block.
fields.amazonItems: Search terms for Amazon links. Empty list = no Amazon item and no kit button.
fields.safety: Exact warnings from the card. Always rendered. Never soften or paraphrase.

ideas.title: Movie Night Popcorn Patrol
steps: Sit the elf on the sofa or on the coffee table, holding the remote.
Put the bowl of popcorn next to it, with a few pieces “spilled” on purpose.
Card: “I picked the movie tonight. You bring the blankets!”

elfNote.text: I picked the movie tonight. You bring the blankets!

ideas.illustrationBrief: Sofa seen from the front, elf in the center holding a remote bigger than the elf, bowl of popcorn beside it with 3 pieces fallen and a folded blanket; simple night-blue background and a clean band at the top for the pin title.

ideas.title: Storytime Reading Corner
steps: Set up a little corner with the pillow.
Elf sitting with the book open on its lap, stuffed animals in a half circle, listening.
Card: “Storytime at the North Pole starts with this one.”

elfNote.text: Storytime at the North Pole starts with this one.

ideas.illustrationBrief: Reading corner seen from the front: elf sitting on the pillow with the book open on its lap and 2 stuffed animals in a half circle, backs to the viewer; cream bedroom background, no extra furniture.

ideas.title: Shoe-Shoe Train
materials: 3 to 4 family shoes in a row
steps: Line up the shoes like train cars in the hallway.
Elf in the first shoe as the engineer, one stuffed animal in each “car”.
Card: “All aboard the North Pole Express! Next stop: breakfast.”

elfNote.text: All aboard the North Pole Express! Next stop: breakfast.

ideas.illustrationBrief: Low side view of the row of 3-4 shoes as train cars, elf engineer in the first shoe and one stuffed animal per car; simple hallway, gold jingle bells on 2 cars.

ideas.title: Toothbrush Delivery Elf
materials: new kids' toothbrush (ideally a themed one)
steps: Tie the bow on the new toothbrush.
Elf sitting on the sink holding the toothbrush like a trophy.
Card: “Santa checks smiles too. New brush, day one!”

elfNote.text: Santa checks smiles too. New brush, day one!

ideas.illustrationBrief: Bathroom sink from the front, elf sitting and holding the new toothbrush upright like a trophy, with a red bow; mirror behind with only the blurred reflection of the hat - no text on the mirror.

ideas.title: Tangled in Christmas Lights
materials: short string of battery-powered LED lights (never plugged into a wall outlet with the child nearby)
steps: Wrap the string loosely around the elf, as if it had fallen while decorating.
Leave the end with the battery box visible, as “proof” of the mischief.
Card: “Decorating is harder than it looks. Help?”
safety: Battery-powered LED lights only - never plugged into a wall outlet with the child nearby.

elfNote.text: Decorating is harder than it looks. Help?

ideas.illustrationBrief: Elf sitting on the floor, wrapped in loose loops of the light string with lit gold bulbs, battery box visible beside it; darkened living-room background in navy blue.

ideas.title: Hiding in the Christmas Tree
materials: just the elf and a sturdy tree branch
steps: Hide the elf among the branches, at the child's eye level, with only the head and one arm sticking out.
No card: the fun is that the child takes a while to find it.
Variation: move to a different branch the next night and turn it into a 2-day hunt.
ideas.variation: Move the elf to a different branch the next night and turn it into a 2-day hunt.
ideas.illustrationBrief: Whole tree in a vertical frame, elf hidden among the branches at mid-height, only head and one little arm out; second version as a close-up of the same branch for the page carousel.
editorNotes: The card says “no card” for this idea: no elf note block.
The second close-up illustration for a carousel is out of the MVP (one illustration per idea).

ideas.title: Letter to Santa Station
steps: Set up the station on the table with everything organized.
Elf holding a mini envelope addressed “To: Santa, North Pole”.
A card inviting the child to write their own letter that day - you collect it and “mail” it at night.
ideas.illustrationBrief: Top view (illustrated flat lay) of the table: paper, envelope, colored pencils and mailbox in an organized grid, elf holding the mini envelope in the bottom corner.
editorNotes: The PDF describes a card but gives no wording: no elf note block until Marketing drafts one (Phase 4).

ideas.title: Trapped in a Jar
materials: large clear glass or plastic jar, with the lid left open
steps: Sit the elf inside the open jar, on the counter.
Rest its little hands against the glass.
Card on the outside: “I climbed in for a cookie. I regret nothing. Please let me out.”

elfNote.text: I climbed in for a cookie. I regret nothing. Please let me out.

ideas.illustrationBrief: Front close-up of the open clear jar on the counter, elf sitting inside with its little hands against the glass and the little card propped outside, facing the viewer.

ideas.title: Christmas Countdown Chain
materials: strips of red and green paper
steps: Make a chain with as many links as there are days left until Christmas.
Elf holding the first link and the scissors (closed, decorative).
Card: “Tear off one link every morning. When the chain is gone... he is coming!”
safety: Glue or stapler: adult use only.

elfNote.text: Tear off one link every morning. When the chain is gone... he is coming!

ideas.illustrationBrief: Red and green paper chain coming down diagonally across the door, elf at the top holding the first link; count the links in the illustration so they match the days left.
editorNotes: Step 2 mentions closed, decorative scissors that are not in the materials list. Never draw scissors in use.

ideas.title: Sleeping in a Stocking
materials: cotton or a small handkerchief as a blanket
steps: Tuck the elf inside the stocking, with only the head out.
Cotton on the edge as a pillow.
Minimal card: “Zzz... five more minutes.” - the perfect idea for the night you almost forgot.

elfNote.text: Zzz... five more minutes.

ideas.illustrationBrief: Close-up of the hanging Christmas stocking, elf inside with only the head out and cotton on the edge as a pillow; tree in the background only as out-of-focus spots of light.

ideas.title: Flour Snow Angel
steps: Spread the flour on the tray - the tray contains the mess and makes cleanup easier.
Lay the elf down and move its arms and legs to draw the angel, then sit it next to its work.
Card: “It snowed in your kitchen last night. I checked.”

elfNote.text: It snowed in your kitchen last night. I checked.

ideas.illustrationBrief: Top view of the shallow tray: angel drawn in the flour in the center and elf sitting on the edge, proud, with flour on its hands; it is the sister scene of the cover - keep the same tray and the same light.

ideas.title: Toilet Paper Tree Makeover
steps: Wrap the paper around the tree like a disastrous garland, leaving loose ends hanging.
Elf at the top holding the roll, as if caught in the act.
Card: “I helped decorate. You are welcome.”

elfNote.text: I helped decorate. You are welcome.

ideas.illustrationBrief: Whole tree wrapped in a messy spiral band of toilet paper, elf at the top holding the roll; leave the top third clean for the pin title.
editorNotes: PDF: no Amazon item - “100% stuff you have” badge. PDF: this one goes to /funny/, not /no-mess/.

ideas.title: Marshmallow Bubble Bath
materials: a bowl or the clean sink
steps: Fill the bowl/sink with marshmallows as if they were foam.
Elf reclining in the middle, only head and feet out.
Card: “North Pole spa day. Do not disturb.”

elfNote.text: North Pole spa day. Do not disturb.

ideas.illustrationBrief: Top view of the bowl-sink full of marshmallows as foam, elf reclining in the middle with only head and feet out and the yellow duck beside it.
editorNotes: PDF: mini marshmallows are the central item of the kit.

ideas.title: Toothpaste Mirror Message
steps: With a finger or a cotton swab, write a short message in a thin layer of toothpaste in the corner of the mirror: “BRUSH! - your elf”.
Elf sitting on the sink holding the open toothpaste.
Cleanup the next day: warm water and paper.
safety: Cleanup the next day: warm water and paper.

elfNote.text: BRUSH! - your elf

ideas.illustrationBrief: Bathroom mirror with the word BRUSH! handwritten in the corner (text drawn on the text layer, never AI-generated), elf sitting on the sink holding the open toothpaste tube.
editorNotes: PDF aside removed from step 3: “say this on the page, parents will thank you”. PDF: no Amazon item - household materials.

ideas.title: Silly Banana Bunch
steps: Draw a different face on each banana: sleepy, startled, laughing.
Elf sitting in the fruit bowl holding the pen.
Card: “The bananas were boring. I fixed them.” - the bananas become the snack of the day.

elfNote.text: The bananas were boring. I fixed them.

ideas.illustrationBrief: Close-up of the bunch with 4-5 bananas, each with a different face, elf sitting in the fruit bowl holding the pen; kitchen background in 2 flat colors.

ideas.title: Sink Fishing Trip
materials: bowl with a little water or blue paper
steps: Make the rod with the string and the paper clip.
Elf sitting on the edge of the sink/bowl, “fishing”.
Scatter the little fish in the “water” and put 2 or 3 already “caught” beside the elf.
ideas.illustrationBrief: Side view of the sink: elf on the edge holding the little rod diagonally over the blue bowl, 3 golden fish in the water and 2 already caught on a small plate beside it.
editorNotes: No card in the PDF: no elf note block until Marketing drafts one (Phase 4).

ideas.title: Sticky Note Surprise Wall
steps: Stick the notes on the door in the shape of a Christmas tree or a big star.
On 3 or 4 notes, write short compliments for the child.
Elf sitting under the “artwork” with the marker in hand.
ideas.illustrationBrief: Door from the front, whole in the vertical frame: colored sticky notes forming a tree, elf sitting underneath with the marker; leave 3-4 notes blank to receive the compliments on the text layer.
editorNotes: No card in the PDF: no elf note block until Marketing drafts one (Phase 4).

ideas.title: Elf Zipline Adventure
materials: a candy cane as the hook
steps: Stretch the line diagonally, nice and tight, out of the way of where people walk.
Hang the elf by the candy cane passed under its arms, in the middle of the run.
Card: “Fastest way to the cookies. Science.”
safety: Stretch the line nice and tight, out of the way of where people walk.

elfNote.text: Fastest way to the cookies. Science.

ideas.illustrationBrief: Strong diagonal from corner to corner: zipline string crossing the living room, elf hanging by the candy cane in the middle of the run, simplified sofa and bookshelf at the ends.
editorNotes: The PDF overview table lists “mini zipline kit / clips”; the card lists candy canes. The card wins.

ideas.title: Sweet Spaghetti Breakfast
materials: a small plate of cooked spaghetti (leftovers are fine)
steps: Put together a little plate of “elf breakfast” spaghetti, with syrup and sprinkles on top.
Elf sitting behind the plate with a fork bigger than the elf.
Card: “Breakfast at the North Pole is different. Try it?” - the child decides whether to taste it.

elfNote.text: Breakfast at the North Pole is different. Try it?

ideas.illustrationBrief: Close-up of the little plate of spaghetti with syrup and sprinkles, fork bigger than the elf behind the plate; out-of-focus kitchen background in warm tones.

ideas.title: Candy Cane Sled
steps: Two candy canes become the runners; the base goes on top.
Another two form the backrest.
Elf sitting on the sled with the mini presents behind, on cotton “snow”.
safety: Hot glue: adult only.
ideas.illustrationBrief: Profile of the sled on the cotton snow: 2 candy canes as runners, base of sticks, elf sitting with 2 mini presents behind; flat light-blue background.
editorNotes: No card in the PDF: no elf note block until Marketing drafts one (Phase 4).
PDF: most clickable kit on the list. Step 3 uses cotton, which is not in the materials list.

ideas.title: Hot Cocoa Stand Helper
steps: Set up a mini stand: small sign reading “ELF COCOA - 1 HUG”.
Elf behind the mug as the server, marshmallows in a little pot beside it.
In the morning, the family makes the hot chocolate together - the idea becomes an activity, not just a scene.

elfNote.text: ELF COCOA - 1 HUG

ideas.illustrationBrief: Mini stand from the front: blank sign at the top (the text ELF COCOA - 1 HUG goes on the text layer), elf behind the mug as the server and a little pot of marshmallows beside it.

ideas.title: Cookie Baking Disaster
materials: a pinch of flour on the counter
rolling pin (a mini one or your own)
steps: Flour spread on just one corner of the counter, and little footprints leading to the elf.
Elf sitting holding the cutter, a bitten cookie beside it.
Card: “Quality control. The cookies passed.”

elfNote.text: Quality control. The cookies passed.

ideas.illustrationBrief: Counter seen diagonally: trail of little flour footprints up to the elf, who holds the cutter with a bitten cookie beside it; keep the flour in just one corner of the frame.

ideas.title: Milk and Cookies Taste Test
materials: paper score sheet with stars to color in
steps: A row of cookies numbered 1 to 3.
Elf with a pencil over the sheet, “rating” them to practice for the night of the 24th.
The child does the real test at snack time and compares their scores with the elf's.
ideas.illustrationBrief: Top view of the row of 3 numbered cookies, little cups of milk beside them and the rating sheet with blank stars under the elf's pencil.
editorNotes: No card in the PDF: no elf note block until Marketing drafts one (Phase 4).
PDF: the affiliate slot is the site's own printable rating sheet, not an Amazon item.

ideas.title: Gingerbread House Inspector
materials: the family's gingerbread house (or a large cookie)
steps: Elf next to the house with the “official inspection” clipboard.
Checklist on the paper: “Walls: strong. Roof: delicious. Approved!”
If there is no house, the elf inspects any cookie - the joke still works.

elfNote.text: Walls: strong. Roof: delicious. Approved!

ideas.illustrationBrief: Scale contrast: large gingerbread house filling half the frame, small elf beside it with clipboard and magnifying glass; clipboard checklist left blank for the text layer.
editorNotes: PDF: highest-ticket kit on the list.

ideas.title: Kindness Mission Card
materials: a card (printable from the site or handmade)
steps: Elf holding the “TOP SECRET MISSION” envelope.
Inside, the mission of the day: “Today: draw a picture for someone you love.”
Rotation of simple missions: help set the table, donate a toy, say thank you to someone.

elfNote.text: Today: draw a picture for someone you love.

ideas.illustrationBrief: Large envelope in the foreground with the TOP SECRET stamp (text on the text layer), elf peeking from behind it; simple bedroom background, no distractions.
editorNotes: PDF: no Amazon item - this idea is the entry point to the site's own printables pack. Envelope label: TOP SECRET MISSION.

ideas.title: Candy Cane Scavenger Hunt
steps: Hide 5 candy canes in places that are visible for the child's age (nothing up high or inside furniture).
Elf at the entrance with the card: “I hid 5 candy canes. Can you find them all before breakfast?”
Toddler variation: 3 candy canes, all in the same room.
safety: Hide them in places visible for the child's age - nothing up high or inside furniture.

elfNote.text: I hid 5 candy canes. Can you find them all before breakfast?

ideas.variation: Toddler version: 3 candy canes, all in the same room.
ideas.illustrationBrief: Wide living room with 1 candy cane visible behind the cushion in the foreground and the elf at the entrance with the count card; the other 4 stay out of frame.

ideas.title: Build-a-Snowman Challenge
materials: a finished mini snowman as the “example”
steps: Build a marshmallow snowman and sit the elf beside it, proud.
Leave a second kit unassembled with the card: “My record is 2 minutes. Beat it!”
The child builds their own at breakfast - and eats the result.

elfNote.text: My record is 2 minutes. Beat it!

ideas.illustrationBrief: Two snowmen side by side on the table: the finished marshmallow one and the unassembled kit (3 marshmallows, toothpicks, sprinkles), elf sitting between the two pointing at the kit.
editorNotes: The PDF overview table lists “marshmallow / toothpick kit”; the card lists large marshmallows. The card wins.

ideas.title: Nice List Certificate
steps: Fill in the certificate with the child's name and one specific quality of theirs this year.
Roll it up like a diploma with the ribbon.
Elf sleeping on the diploma on the bed or at the bedroom door, so it is the first thing seen on waking up.
ideas.illustrationBrief: Diploma unrolled diagonally on the bed, gold ribbon beside it and elf sleeping on its corner; name area left blank - never generate a name in the image.
editorNotes: No card in the PDF - the certificate is the message. No elf note block. PDF: the file is the site's own product.

ideas.title: Would You Rather Card
materials: a card with a “would you rather?” question (printable from the site)
steps: Elf in the child's seat at the table, holding the card: “Would you rather ride a reindeer or drive the sleigh?”
The family answers at breakfast; the answer becomes the next day's card, in a cycle that lasts the whole season.
A series of 24 questions makes one printable set.

elfNote.text: Would you rather ride a reindeer or drive the sleigh?

ideas.illustrationBrief: Breakfast table from the front: elf in the child's seat holding a large blank card (the question goes on the text layer), simplified cup and plate beside it.
editorNotes: PDF aside removed from step 3: the 24-question printable “feeds the daily email”. PDF: no Amazon item - own printable.
The PDF gives 1 question; the other 23 are drafted by Marketing in Phase 4 for approval.

ideas.title: Farewell Letter and Photo
materials: the favorite photo of the season
steps: On the morning of the 24th, elf sitting by the tree with the letter: it says thank you, mentions 2 real moments of the child's year and promises to come back.
The frame with the photo becomes the keepsake that stays all year.
At night, the elf “leaves” - the letter explains that only Santa can touch the elf at the farewell, settling the no-touching rule with affection.
ideas.illustrationBrief: Under the tree at night: open letter and frame with the silhouette of the favorite photo (no real child's face), elf sitting between the two with the tree lights as gold dots in the background.
editorNotes: The PDF gives no letter wording: no elf note block; Marketing drafts the farewell letter in Phase 4 for approval.

ideas.title: I'm Back! Arrival Banner
steps: Put up the banner on the wall or on the living-room door the night before the arrival, with the name space left blank.
Elf sitting under the banner holding the marker, as if it had just finished writing.
Card: “I'm back! I missed you all year. Let the December fun begin!”

elfNote.text: I'm back! I missed you all year. Let the December fun begin!

ideas.illustrationBrief: Living-room wall from the front: blank banner in an arc at the top (the text goes on the text layer), elf underneath holding the marker, little bells at the ends of the string.
editorNotes: PDF aside removed from step 1: the blank name space is “for the site's text layer”.

ideas.title: North Pole Arrival Breakfast
materials: mini pancakes (ready-made or from a mix)
steps: On the morning of the arrival, put together a little plate of mini pancakes with strawberry and whipped cream - an elf-sized portion.
Elf behind the plate with the welcome sign.
Card: “Breakfast is on me today. North Pole recipe - extra tiny!” The family makes the big version together.

elfNote.text: Breakfast is on me today. North Pole recipe - extra tiny!

ideas.illustrationBrief: Kitchen table from the front: stack of mini pancakes with strawberry on the little plate, elf behind it holding the blank sign, small cup beside it; bright morning light.

ideas.title: Special Delivery Arrival Box
steps: Line the box with cotton like a nest and sit the elf inside, with only the head out.
Close the flaps halfway and tie with string, without pulling tight.
Tag: “Special Delivery - From: North Pole. Handle with giggles.” Leave the box at the front door.

elfNote.text: Special Delivery - From: North Pole. Handle with giggles.

ideas.illustrationBrief: Open kraft paper box at the front door, elf inside on the cotton with only the head out, string in a bow beside it and a blank tag facing the viewer.
editorNotes: PDF aside removed from step 3: the tag text goes “on the site's text layer”.

ideas.title: Arrival Hide-and-Seek Clue Trail
materials: 1 jingle bell at the final hiding spot
steps: Hide the elf somewhere visible for the child's age (bookshelf, tree, low shelf) with the jingle bell beside it.
Leave 4 clues in sequence from the bed to the hiding spot, each one pointing to the next room.
Starting card: “I'm back... but where? Follow the clues and find me before breakfast!”

elfNote.text: I'm back... but where? Follow the clues and find me before breakfast!

ideas.illustrationBrief: Hallway in perspective: 3 blank cards on the floor in a curved trail and, in the background, the elf peeking from behind the tree with a little bell beside it.
editorNotes: PDF: printable clue cards are the site's own digital product; card stock is the Amazon search.

ideas.title: Snowy Footprints Arrival
materials: 1 spoonful of flour or powdered sugar
a paper footprint stencil (or the sole of the elf's own foot)
steps: Hold the stencil against the mat and sift a thin layer of flour only inside it, making 4-5 footprints from the door into the house.
Sit the elf at the end of the trail, with flour on its little feet.
Card: “Snow on my boots! Sorry about the footprints - I was too excited to wait.” Cleanup: vacuum the mat, 2 minutes.

elfNote.text: Snow on my boots! Sorry about the footprints - I was too excited to wait.

ideas.illustrationBrief: Top view of the doormat: trail of 5 little white footprints curving from the door to the elf sitting at the end, with floured little feet; door ajar in the background.

ideas.title: Toddler Peekaboo Blanket Fort
steps: A simple, safe little fort with the blanket over the sofa - nothing heavy in the structure.
Elf inside, peeking through the opening with one little hand.
Minimal card, to read aloud: “Peekaboo! I see you!” The game of the day is finding and re-hiding the elf together.
safety: Simple, safe fort - nothing heavy in the structure.

elfNote.text: Peekaboo! I see you!

ideas.illustrationBrief: Blanket fort over the sofa seen from the front, elf peeking through the opening in the center and 2 large stuffed animals sitting as the audience; big shapes and few objects, toddler standard.

ideas.title: Pom-Pom Color Sorting Game
materials: large pom-poms (a size that is safe for the child's age, always with supervision)
steps: On the tray, leave half of the pom-poms already sorted by color in the 3 cups, as an example.
Elf holding a pom-pom over the right cup, mid-game.
Card: “I sorted mine by color. Can you finish the rest?” No small parts for children under 3.
safety: Large pom-poms only, a size that is safe for the child's age, always with supervision.
No small parts for children under 3.

elfNote.text: I sorted mine by color. Can you finish the rest?

ideas.illustrationBrief: Top view of the tray: 3 colored cups in a row, large pom-poms already sorted into 2 cups and the elf holding a pom-pom over the third; very distinct primary colors.

ideas.title: Breakfast Cereal Garland
steps: A short garland already started by the adult (6-8 rings on the thread), wrapped around the elf like a necklace.
Bowl of cereal beside it, for the child to continue at breakfast - and eat the result.
Card: “I made you a necklace for breakfast. You can eat it!” Always with supervision.
safety: Always with supervision.

elfNote.text: I made you a necklace for breakfast. You can eat it!

ideas.illustrationBrief: Elf on the kitchen table wearing the ring garland as a necklace that is too big, small bowl beside it; simple scene, 3 objects at most.

ideas.title: My First Sticker Scene
materials: large sheet of paper or poster board
steps: Draw just the outline of a big tree on the poster board and stick on 2-3 stickers as an example.
Elf sitting beside it holding a star sticker, at the top of the tree that it cannot reach.
Card: “I started our picture. The star is too high - can you help me?” The child completes the scene that day.

elfNote.text: I started our picture. The star is too high - can you help me?

ideas.illustrationBrief: Large poster board seen from the front: simple tree outline, 3 stickers already on and the elf standing on a little chair holding the star, not reaching the top.

ideas.title: Toy Car Wash Station
steps: On the towel: basin with two fingers of water, one car inside and another waiting in line.
Elf on the edge of the basin holding the little brush, as the attendant.
Card: “Car wash open! Dirty toy cars welcome.” Water only with an adult present, the whole time.
safety: Water only with an adult present, the whole time.

elfNote.text: Car wash open! Dirty toy cars welcome.

ideas.illustrationBrief: Basin on the towel, from the front: a large toy car in the water with simple bubbles, another in line and the elf on the edge with the little brush.

ideas.title: Plush Friends Campout
materials: a small cloth or mini blanket for each stuffed animal
a small flashlight, switched off, or a toy one
steps: Wrap each stuffed animal in its cloth like a sleeping bag, in a row on the bedroom floor.
Elf in the middle of the row, wrapped up too, with only the head out.
Minimal card: “Sleepover! We camped in your room.” - a calm scene, designed not to stir things up before bedtime.

elfNote.text: Sleepover! We camped in your room.

ideas.illustrationBrief: Row of 3 improvised sleeping bags on the floor: stuffed animal, elf in the middle with only the head out, and stuffed animal; switched-off flashlight beside them.

ideas.title: Fruit Face Breakfast Plate
materials: large blueberries cut in half (toddler safety)
steps: Make a face on the plate: pancake for the face, banana for the hair, strawberries for the cheeks.
Elf beside it holding a strawberry, as co-author.
Card: “Breakfast was boring. I gave it a face!” Round fruit always cut in half.
safety: Round fruit always cut in half. Large blueberries cut in half (toddler safety).

elfNote.text: Breakfast was boring. I gave it a face!

ideas.illustrationBrief: Top view of the plate: pancake face with banana hair and strawberry cheeks, elf sitting on the rim of the plate holding a strawberry; light, clean table background.
editorNotes: PDF aside removed from step 3: cutting round fruit in half is “a rule of the page”.

ideas.title: Elf Workshop Build Station
materials: wooden blocks or large building pieces
steps: Set up the workbench: blocks as a shelf, tools in a row and the half-built toy in the center - a 15-20 minute project, no rush.
Elf in a paper hard hat on the toy, holding the little wrench.
Card: “Workshop shift started. This toy will be ready by Christmas - probably.”

elfNote.text: Workshop shift started. This toy will be ready by Christmas - probably.

ideas.illustrationBrief: Miniature workbench, from the front: shelf of blocks, tools in a row, half-built toy in the center and the elf in a paper hard hat on top of it.

ideas.title: Paper Snowflake Window Invasion
steps: Fold and cut out 8-12 snowflakes of different sizes - scissors for the adult only, about 20 minutes in total.
Hang them on the window or on a string across the living room, from largest to smallest.
Elf on the windowsill holding a snowflake bigger than the elf. Card: “I ordered snow. This was the delivery.”
safety: Scissors are for the adult only.

elfNote.text: I ordered snow. This was the delivery.

ideas.illustrationBrief: Window taken over by 10 paper snowflakes of different sizes on strings, elf on the windowsill holding a huge snowflake.
editorNotes: KNOWN CORRECTION: the scissors stay as an Amazon search only. Cutting is an ADULT-ONLY step. Never suggest scissors for a child anywhere on the page.

ideas.title: Mini Elf Door and Welcome Mat
materials: cardboard or thin wood for the little door
steps: Cut out and assemble the little door (about 15 cm / 6 in) with a jingle-bell doorknob - the longest project on the list, about 25 minutes including drying time.
Attach it to the baseboard at the entrance or in the bedroom, with the little mat in front.
Elf on the mat, as if it had arrived through its own door. Card: “I finally got my own door. Please knock.”

elfNote.text: I finally got my own door. Please knock.

ideas.illustrationBrief: Close-up of the wall baseboard: little red arched door with a jingle-bell knob, patterned little mat in front and the elf sitting on it; keep the door closed - the mystery is the fun.
editorNotes: The inch conversion (6 in) was added for the US audience; the PDF gives 15 cm.

ideas.title: Cardboard Sleigh Build
steps: Cover the box in red and build the curved front of the sleigh with another piece of cardboard - about 20 minutes; the child decorates it the next day.
Candy canes as runners and cotton as the seat.
Elf in the sleigh holding the string reins. Card: “Test-driving the backup sleigh. It passed. Mostly.”

elfNote.text: Test-driving the backup sleigh. It passed. Mostly.

ideas.illustrationBrief: Cardboard sleigh covered in red in three-quarter profile, candy cane runners, cotton on the seat and the elf holding the string reins; simple living-room background.

ideas.title: Gingerbread Village Street
materials: 3-4 mini gingerbread houses (kit or large cookies)
a cardboard base covered in white
steps: Build the street on the base: houses on both sides, a sprinkle path down the middle - 20 minutes, the icing needs to set.
Elf in the middle of the street with the little clipboard, now mayor of the village.
Card: “Welcome to Gingerbread Lane. I am the mayor now.” The village decorates the table until the 24th.

elfNote.text: Welcome to Gingerbread Lane. I am the mayor now.

ideas.illustrationBrief: Little street in three-quarter view: 4 houses in 2 rows, sprinkle path in the center and the elf with a clipboard in the middle; sugar snow at the edges.

ideas.title: Elf Photo Booth Props
materials: sticks with a paper mustache, hat and antlers
steps: Set up the corner in the living room: frame leaning against the wall and the props in a little pot.
Elf inside the frame wearing the paper mustache, posing.
Card: “Photo booth is open! Your turn - you're the model today.” The family uses the same setup in the morning.

elfNote.text: Photo booth is open! Your turn - you're the model today.

ideas.illustrationBrief: Gold cardboard frame leaning against the wall, elf inside it wearing a paper mustache that is too big, little pot with paper hat and antlers beside it; flat background for cutout.

ideas.title: Elf Story Mad Libs Card
materials: card with a mini story with 5 blanks
steps: Card on the breakfast table, elf holding the pencil over the first blank.
The story starts ready-made: “Last night, the elf rode a ___ to the ___ ...” - the blanks ask for a noun, a place, a food, an animal and a verb.
Card: “I wrote my story but forgot the best words. Fill the blanks at breakfast!”

elfNote.text: I wrote my story but forgot the best words. Fill the blanks at breakfast!

ideas.illustrationBrief: Large card on the table in three-quarter view, 5 clearly visible blank lines (no generated text in the image), pencil on the first line and the elf holding its tip.
editorNotes: PDF: printable story cards are the site's own digital product; card stock is the Amazon search.
TRADEMARK FLAG: the title contains “Mad Libs”, a registered trademark of a third party. Title kept as in the PDF pending the owner's decision.

ideas.title: Elf Workout Challenge Cards
materials: 3 challenge cards (jump 10 times, spin 3 times, balance on one foot)
steps: Elf on the little mat in an impossible yoga pose, 3 cards fanned out in front.
Each card: a 30-second challenge for the family to do together at breakfast.
Card: “North Pole training! Can you do all 3 before breakfast? I did the first one. Sort of.”

elfNote.text: North Pole training! Can you do all 3 before breakfast? I did the first one. Sort of.

ideas.illustrationBrief: Elf toppled over in an exaggerated yoga pose on the little mat, 3 blank cards fanned out in front of it and a cushion beside it; living room with lots of empty space around.
editorNotes: PDF: printable challenge cards are the site's own digital product; the exercise mat is the Amazon search.

ideas.title: Guess How Many Jar
materials: clear jar with a tightly closed lid
candies or marshmallows, counted (write down the number)
steps: Count the contents, write the number on a folded piece of paper and close the jar - sealed all day.
Elf on the lid holding its own slip, with an absurd guess.
Card: “Guess how many! Winner picks tonight's Christmas song.” The result comes at dinner, with the folded paper as proof.

elfNote.text: Guess how many! Winner picks tonight's Christmas song.

ideas.illustrationBrief: Clear jar full of marshmallows on the counter, lid closed, elf on top of it with a blank slip and 3 slips beside it.

ideas.title: Draw My Outfit Contest
materials: sheet with the elf outline to color (printable from the site)
steps: Leave the elf outline on the table with one part already colored by the elf: one foot of each color, on purpose.
Elf sitting on the sheet holding the red pencil.
Card: “Design my new outfit! Best drawing goes on the fridge tonight.” The winner gets the fridge that same night.

elfNote.text: Design my new outfit! Best drawing goes on the fridge tonight.

ideas.illustrationBrief: Top view of the sheet with the elf outline: one foot red, the other green, colored pencils in an arc and the elf in the corner holding a pencil.

ideas.title: Flour Snowball Fight
steps: WARNING: high mess, only inside the tray. Battlefield on the tray: a flour trench, stuffed animals on one side, elf on the other behind the cotton fort.
Snowballs in the air of the scene and flour on the elf's little arms, caught in the act.
Card: “Snowball fight! The teddies started it.” Tray goes straight to the sink - a 5-minute cleanup.
safety: WARNING: high mess, only inside the tray.
Tray goes straight to the sink - a 5-minute cleanup.

elfNote.text: Snowball fight! The teddies started it.

ideas.illustrationBrief: High-rimmed tray in three-quarter view: cotton fort with the elf behind it, 2 stuffed animals on the other side, little balls in the air in an arc and flour only inside the tray.
editorNotes: PDF aside removed from step 3: the 5-minute cleanup is “stated on the page”.

ideas.title: Bubble Bath Foam Mountain
steps: WARNING: high and wet mess - towel on the floor before anything else. Sink full of real foam until it forms a mountain.
Elf at the top, in a paper shower cap, duck sliding down beside it.
Card: “I asked for a little foam. A LITTLE.” Drain and rinse the same morning.
safety: WARNING: high and wet mess - towel on the floor before anything else.
Drain and rinse the same morning.

elfNote.text: I asked for a little foam. A LITTLE.

ideas.illustrationBrief: Sink overflowing with a round mountain of white foam, elf in a paper shower cap sitting at the top and the yellow duck sliding down the side; towel visible on the floor.

ideas.title: Wrapping Paper Mayhem
materials: 3-4 living-room objects (cushion, remote, empty vase, book)
steps: WARNING: the most time-consuming idea on the list (15+ minutes). Wrap 3-4 living-room objects as perfect presents, bow and all.
Elf on the wrapped remote, holding the end of the paper and the tape.

Card: “I wrapped everything for Santa. You're welcome. Unwrap carefully.” The scene is meant to be the first thing seen on entering the living room - it lasts minutes, until someone unwraps the first object.

elfNote.text: I wrapped everything for Santa. You're welcome. Unwrap carefully.

ideas.illustrationBrief: Living room with cushion, book and remote wrapped with bows, elf on the remote holding the end of an open roll that crosses the frame.
editorNotes: PDF aside removed from step 1: this is also “the idea with the highest viral potential”.

ideas.title: Elf in the Fridge Surprise
materials: clean, dry little plate or container
a little paper or ribbon scarf
steps: Hygiene first: elf on a clean, dry little plate, never directly on food, away from open food.
Plate on the shelf at the child's eye level, elf wrapped in the scarf, shivering.
Card outside the door: “It's SO cold in the North Pole. I came to compare.” Remove it the same morning.
safety: Hygiene first: elf on a clean, dry little plate, never directly on food, away from open food.
Remove it the same morning.

elfNote.text: It's SO cold in the North Pole. I came to compare.

ideas.illustrationBrief: Fridge interior from the front, door open: elf on a clean little plate in a big scarf, between closed containers and simple bottles; no open food.

ideas.title: Fridge Magnet Message
steps: A short phrase with the magnets at the child's height: 3-5 words, a compliment or the countdown of days.
Elf at the bottom edge of the door holding the last letter, out of place.
Card: “One letter is missing on purpose. Can you finish my message?” For Kids - magnets are not for toddlers.
safety: For Kids - magnets are not for toddlers.

elfNote.text: One letter is missing on purpose. Can you finish my message?

ideas.illustrationBrief: Fridge door from the front: row of letter magnets with an empty space at the end (letters on the text layer), elf below holding the missing letter.

ideas.title: Closet Fashion Show Elf
materials: a paper runway or an open book
steps: Runway in the bedroom: open book or strip of paper on the floor, little clothes on a string clothesline in the background.
Elf in the middle wearing the most over-the-top piece (big hat, scarf down to the floor).
Card: “Fashion week, North Pole edition. This is the look.” Change the piece the next night: a 2-day series.

elfNote.text: Fashion week, North Pole edition. This is the look.

ideas.illustrationBrief: Paper runway on the floor in perspective, little clothesline in the background with 3 outfits and the elf in the center in a huge hat and a dragging scarf.

ideas.title: Memory Jar - Last Week Goodbye
steps: In the last week (from the 18th on), jar in the living room with the cards beside it and the elf holding the first one, already with a memory of its own.
Each day the family writes a memory and puts it in the jar; the elf brings a new card each night.
Card: “Before I go, let's save our favorite moments. I started - your turn tonight.” The jar comes back with the elf the following year.

elfNote.text: Before I go, let's save our favorite moments. I started - your turn tonight.

ideas.illustrationBrief: Nearly empty clear jar on the living-room table, 2 cards inside, fan of blank cards beside it and the elf with a card of wavy lines (no generated text).

ideas.title: Goodbye Breakfast and Hug Coupon
materials: a paper hug coupon (printable coupon from the site)
steps: On the morning of the 24th or 25th, set the table with the elf's place: little plate, heart cookie and the hug coupon in the mug.
Elf in its place with the short see-you-soon letter - different from the long letter in idea 30, this one is for the table, for breakfast.
Coupon text: “One goodbye hug - good for today only. Love, your elf. See you next Christmas!” The goodbye hug is the exception to the no-touching rule, explained in the letter.

elfNote.text: One goodbye hug - good for today only. Love, your elf. See you next Christmas!

ideas.illustrationBrief: Breakfast table in three-quarter view: place set for the elf with a little plate, heart-shaped cookie and a blank coupon propped on the mug (the text goes on the text layer), elf holding a little letter.
